svg.title: CueGlass — proposed design concept board (not a screenshot)
svg.desc: Persisted design research artifact. Final adopted design uses whole-window alpha, a separate text-panel opacity, and a 420 by 124 Controls panel with fine and jump buttons. This board is a proposal, never actual application evidence.
svg.text: PROPOSED DESIGN · NOT A SCREENSHOT · not user-tested · macOS 14 baseline (no Liquid Glass APIs) · operator UI follows system appearance; light shown
Numbers ① – ⑩ map to report §4. Sizes in points.
🔒 Editing locked during the take · Stop Take to edit

g.text: Good morning, and thank you all for
being here. Today is about one simple
idea: tools should get out of the way.
When you record at your desk, the
words should sit right under the camera
— calm, legible, and at your pace.
So we built three things. First, a
prompter that reads like a page. Second,
controls you can reach without looking.
Third, timing you can trust, so you
always know how much is left.
Let’s begin with the page itself.

svg.text: ⑧ Controls panel (R11) — NSPanel, HUD material, 360 × 116

g.text: Fades to 0 while playing only if “Hide controls while playing” is on;
returns on pause or pointer movement (instant when Reduce Motion is on).
Reduce Transparency → opaque #1C1C1E. Title “Controls”, no minimize button.

svg.text: ⑨ Floating Prompter (R10) — top-centre under the camera, 40 % × 30 % of screen, 85 %

PLAYING — no chrome. Optional click-through; Esc, Controls panel and menu always regain control.

Adopted qualification: whole-window opacity 30–100 % (default 85 %); separate text-panel opacity 0–100 %; warn below 4.5 : 1

svg.text: Proposed design concept for CueGlass (working name CueFlow). Drawn as SVG by the design advisor, 2026-10-13. Fonts render with the viewer’s system font; colour values for system colours are illustrative, never hard-coded.
